newsitem.title: CHINA: China H1 copper, zinc, aluminium consumption up.
newsitem.headline: China H1 copper, zinc, aluminium consumption up.

text.p: China's consumption of copper, zinc and aluminium rose in the first half of 1997 compared with the year-ago period, while lead consumption fell, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Monday.
Copper consumption rose a year-on-year 12.8 percent in the first six months, with exports soaring by 92.1 percent to 42,100 tonnes, the newspaper said.

Copper supply totalled 588,800 tonnes, up 5.8 percent from the year-ago period, it said. Domestic output was up 13.1 percent to 503,400 tonnes, while imports were down 23.5 percent to 85,400 tonnes, it said.
Zinc consumption increased 31.3 percent, with exports skyrocketing 140 percent to 48,800 tonnes, it said.

Zinc supply increased 29.8 percent to 729,900 tonnes in the first half, with domestic output rising 30.6 percent to 697,400 tonnes and imports jumping 15.3 percent to 32,500 tonnes, the newspaper said.
Aluminium consumption was up 11.9 percent, the newspaper said without giving comparative figures.
Aluminium supply reached 1.0321 million tonnes by the end of June, up 9.7 percent from the year-ago period, it said.
Lead consumption fell 7.8 percent, with exports down 26.6 percent to 96,100 tonnes, it said.
Lead supply rose 10.3 percent to 294,200 tonnes, with domestic output up 9.1 percent to 287,900 tonnes and imports soaring 120 percent to 6,300 tonnes, it said.

Tin supply inched up 5.6 percent to 29,800 tonnes, with domestic output increasing by four percent to 28,500 tonnes and imports soaring by 61.8 percent to 1,300 tonnes in the first half, the newspaper said without giving further details.
